## How a chiropractic practice started showing up in AI answers
URL: https://simpleesystem.com/blog/chiropractic-practice-ai-answers/

Getting found How a chiropractic practice started showing up in AI answers Jason Claybrook September 30, 2026 Getting found [Photo: real client, real place] Patients now ask ChatGPT and Claude who to see before they search on Google. If your practice isn't in those answers, those patients never reach your front door. CJW Chiropractic Solutions changed that in a few weeks. This is what happened and what other practices can take from it. The starting point Dr. Courtney Williams wanted new patients to find his practice when they asked AI platforms for a chiropractor. The practice was not showing up in those answers. Practices like this face a common problem. A patient asks a platform for a chiropractor near them and gets a short list of names. The patient usually books from that list. A practice that isn't on it doesn't get a chance to compete on price, reviews, or quality. What AI visibility means AI visibility is how often platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok recommend or cite your business when someone asks about a service you offer. A citation is a named mention, often with a link to your site. You can measure it. You ask the platforms the same questions your patients ask and record which businesses they name. That measurement comes first. It shows where you stand today and which local competitors the platforms name instead of you. The platforms draw on what they can read and trust. A site that states its services, location, hours, and insurance answers in plain language gives them something to quote. A site that hides those answers behind vague copy gives them nothing. What we did We started by asking the AI platforms the questions local patients ask about chiropractic care. We recorded the answers and compared them with what nearby practices were getting. Then we built a new site for CJW. It has clear pages for each service, plain headings, and answers placed at the top of each page. It loads fast and carries the business details that search engines and AI platforms read. The site went live in July 2026. We wrote the pages that answer patient questions in Dr. Williams's voice. Nothing went live without his approval. We also put Fred on the site. He works as the front desk and handles hours, services, insurance questions, and booking. He never handles symptoms or medical history. The work followed our 90-day approach. The first 30 days set a baseline next to local competitors. The next 30 fixed the site structure and business information and filled in the answer pages. The last 30 put new content live in his voice, with a first comparison of how the platforms answered before and after. The result AI platforms started citing CJW about six weeks after launch. In the first two months, 10 new patients said they found the practice through ChatGPT and 3 through Claude. That is 13 new patients from AI, on top of patients from search and Fred. "In the first two months, 10 new patients told us they found us through ChatGPT, and 3 more through Claude." Dr. Courtney Williams, CJW Chiropractic Solutions What other practices can take from it Find out where you stand. Ask the AI platforms what your patients ask and see who they name. Answer questions directly. Put the answer in the first lines of each page, then add detail. Keep your business details the same everywhere. Name, address, phone, and hours should match across your site and your listings. Give every service its own page. Platforms cite pages that answer one question well. Give patients an easy next step. A front desk that answers at night and books a visit turns an answer into an appointment. Give it time. CJW was cited about six weeks after launch, not the next day. The work also doesn't stop at launch. After the first 90 days, the real questions patients ask Fred feed the next round of content, so the site keeps answering what people actually want to know. Results vary by market, and we can't promise the same numbers. We can show you where your practice stands. The free AI visibility check asks the platforms your patients' questions and shows the answers next to local competitors. A note on patient privacy Fred does not discuss symptoms or medical history. A patient who raises one is pointed to the office. [one sentence on HIPAA] Keep reading Read the full CJW Chiropractic case study . See how we work with local practices . Learn more about getting found in search and AI answers. Start here See what AI says about your business. Run a free check. We'll show you how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok answer the questions your customers ask, how you compare to local competitors, and what to fix first. ## Why your Bing listing also decides what Yahoo shows
URL: https://simpleesystem.com/blog/yahoo-bing-local-listings/

Getting found Why your Bing listing also decides what Yahoo shows Jason Claybrook September 29, 2026 Getting found Many business owners check their Google listing and stop there. Bing gets less attention, yet one listing there reaches more than Bing itself. It also affects Yahoo, and it can affect what some AI platforms say about you. Yahoo results come from Bing Yahoo search results are powered by Bing. A business that is missing or wrong on Bing is usually missing or wrong on Yahoo too. One complete listing covers both. Many people use Yahoo as their default search, and many use Bing through Windows and Microsoft Edge. You don't need to know how many in your market. You only need to know that a single Bing listing serves all of them. Some AI platforms draw on Bing data Some AI platforms use Bing's search index or data when they look up local businesses. Which platforms do, and how heavily, changes over time. We treat Bing as one of several sources that can shape an AI answer. A correct Bing listing is cheap to maintain and removes one way an AI platform could repeat wrong information about you. This doesn't replace your Google Business Profile. It adds to it. Google remains a major source for local search, and the work you put into a Google profile carries over to Bing because the details are the same. What a complete Bing Places listing includes Bing Places is Microsoft's free tool for business listings. A complete listing has these parts: Business name, exactly as it appears on your sign and website Street address, or a service area if you travel to customers Main phone number Website address Hours, including holiday hours Primary category and any extra categories that fit A short business description Photos of your location, team, and work Services you offer You also need to verify ownership. Until you do, changes may not go live and you can't control what shows. Keep name, address, phone, and hours consistent Search engines and AI platforms compare what they find about your business across many sources. When the name, address, phone number, or hours differ, they have to guess which version is right. Small differences count. "Suite 4" on one listing and "Ste. 4" on another is a mismatch. So is an old phone number on a directory you forgot about. Pick one exact version of each detail. Use it on your website, Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, Nextdoor, and every directory that lists you. Duplicates cause the same trouble. If Bing shows two listings for one location, merge or remove the extra one. Customers and platforms can't tell which is current. Why hours and categories deserve attention Hours are the detail that goes stale fastest. A customer who drives to a closed business after reading wrong hours remembers it, and may leave a review about it. Categories matter because they tell a search engine which searches your business fits. A plumber listed only under a general category can miss searches for drain cleaning or water heaters. Choose the category that matches your main service first, then add others that are true. Descriptions and services deserve the same care. Write them in plain words that match how customers ask. Avoid stuffing in keywords. A short, accurate description helps a person decide, and it gives a platform clean text to reuse. A short checklist Search for your business on Bing and see what appears. Claim or create your Bing Places listing and verify it. Fill in every field, not just the required ones. Match your name, address, phone, and hours to your website. Add photos and a short description. Update hours before each holiday. Recheck every few months, and after any move or phone change. We handle this as part of local listings , along with Google, Apple Maps, Yelp, Nextdoor, and directories. To see how AI platforms describe your business today, run the free AI visibility check . Start here See what AI says about your business. Run a free check. We'll show you how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok answer the questions your customers ask, how you compare to local competitors, and what to fix first. How follow-up works Lead score Your team calls the best leads first Every Fred conversation gets a score. Trust. How much confidence they show in your business. Capacity. Whether they can afford and take on the work. Authority. Whether they are the person who decides. Timeline. ## AI assistants for your business | Simple eSystem
URL: https://simpleesystem.com/engagement/ai-assistants/

AI assistants An AI team member that answers for you around the clock. We deploy Fred on your site. He answers customer questions, books appointments, scores leads, and hands off to your people when it matters. The short answer Fred is an AI team member who answers only from your content and cannot step outside his role. Reputation management Happy customers come back and say so in public. Reviews shape who customers call and who AI platforms recommend. The short answer Reputation management gets more of your happy customers to leave reviews, monitors what people say, and answers each review. Run your AI visibility check Talk to Fred What we do Request, monitor, and respond Reviews requested at the right moment A request goes out soon after a job is done or an appointment ends, when the customer is happiest. Your team sees them quickly and does not have to check each site. Reviews answered Each review gets a reply. Thanks for the good ones. A calm, specific response for the hard ones, with a way to make it right. The research Stars affect revenue A Harvard Business School working paper by Michael Luca studied Yelp ratings and restaurant sales. Each added star lifted revenue 5 to 9 percent for independent restaurants. The study covers independent restaurants, so treat it as evidence that ratings move real money, not as a promise for your trade. It is also why a steady flow of honest reviews is worth building. Timing Why the moment matters A customer is happiest right after the problem is solved. That is when a request gets answered. Asking a week later, or never, leaves reviews to the customers who are upset enough to post on their own. A timely request gives your happy customers a voice too. The request is triggered by the job or visit, so your staff does not have to remember it. Search and AI Reviews feed local search and AI answers Google weighs review count, rating, and freshness for local results. AI platforms read the same public signals when they decide whom to recommend. Recent reviews show a business that is active today. Reviews that name your services and city help platforms match you to real questions. Replies show that a person is paying attention. Reviews work best alongside strong local listings and a site built to answer questions. See search visibility for how they connect. No. Every review comes from a real customer. We ask, we make it easy, and we never write or buy reviews. What happens with a bad review? We flag it to your team quickly and help draft a calm, specific reply. A good response shows future customers how you handle problems. Do reviews affect AI recommendations? Copy We copy the site to our platform. Your live site stays untouched and keeps serving visitors. 3.
